chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the churches (of the Christians), whether it is permissible to demolish them for the construction of mosques, so he said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْبِيَعِ: Churches (specifically of the Christians, singular: بَيْعَة)
key_terms.الْكَنَائِسِ: Churches (plural of كَنِيسَة, often used interchangeably or to denote specific types)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to demolish churches to build mosques in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the perimissibility of demolishing Christian churches to construct mosques, reflecting the juristic view of structural utility rather than permanent displacement. This ruling is often contextualized within the era of Islamic sovereignty where such structures were not under specific protective treaties (*dhimma*) that guaranteed their preservation, distinguishing it from later fiqh discussions on *al-Kanā'is*. The confirmation underscores the precedence of Islamic worship spaces in public religious geography during the early Shia scholarly period.
